plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether constrained local refinement of middle-stack layers can突破 the ~0.818 target score plateau observed in prior iterations. The strategy fixes the outer layers (0-14 and 22-23) from the best previous candidate and focuses optimization on layers 15-21 using Nelder-Mead simplex with ±12 nm bounds. Two uniform-random candidates inject per round to maintain diversity and prevent premature trapping. This is planned from recalled knowledge of dichroic filter design patterns and optimization behavior, not from retrieved literature.

routes.title: Constrained Local Search on 24-Layer HfO2/SiO2 Dichroic with Fixed Outer Layers
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Fixing the outer 17 layers (0-14 and 22-23) from the best prior candidate and optimizing only the middle 7 layers (15-21) with Nelder-Mead simplex refinement will improve the dual-band target score beyond the ~0.818 plateau while maintaining physical validity.
routes.design_principle: In multi-band dichroic stacks, outer layers primarily establish the high-reflectance band edge while inner layers fine-tune transmission band ripple and phase matching. Constraining the search space around a proven topology reduces optimizer wandering while allowing local improvements in the transition region.
routes.proposed_topology: 24-layer alternating stack starting with HfO2 on air side: HfO2/SiO2/HfO2/SiO2/HfO2/SiO2/HfO2/SiO2/HfO2/SiO2/HfO2/SiO2/HfO2/SiO2/HfO2/SiO2/HfO2/SiO2/HfO2/SiO2/HfO2/SiO2/HfO2/SiO2 on fused silica substrate
design_variables: thicknesses of layers 15-21 (7 middle layers) with Nelder-Mead simplex, bounds ±12 nm from baseline; layers 0-14 and 22-23 fixed at baseline values; 2 uniform-random candidates injected per round for diversity
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band
maintain physical validity (no negative thicknesses, no absorption violations)
manufacturing_considerations: all thicknesses within 20-200 nm range for sputter deposition feasibility
material pair HfO2/SiO2 is industry-standard for SWIR dichroics
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: Quarter-wave stacks at band edges create high reflectance; deviation from quarter-wave in transition region controls passband ripple
Recalled knowledge: HfO2 (n~2.0 at 1500 nm) and SiO2 (n~1.45 at 1500 nm) provide adequate index contrast for SWIR dichroics
Recalled knowledge: Nelder-Mead simplex converges well on smooth multi-dimensional thickness spaces when initialized near a local optimum
Recalled knowledge: Fixing outer layers reduces search dimensionality and prevents optimizer from destroying established band-edge performance
expected_advantages: Faster convergence than full 24-layer optimization due to reduced search space (7 vs 24 variables)
Lower risk of degrading the high-reflectance band since outer layers are fixed
Random candidate injection prevents trapping in local minima within the constrained subspace
known_risks: Uncertain whether the plateau at ~0.818 is due to middle-layer limitation or fundamental material/stack constraint - would need full-stack sensitivity analysis to confirm
±12 nm bounds may be too restrictive if optimal solution requires larger deviations - would need to relax bounds if no improvement after 3 rounds
Nelder-Mead may still converge to local optimum within the constrained subspace - random injection mitigates but does not eliminate this risk
Refractive index dispersion of HfO2 and SiO2 across 300-1700 nm is recalled approximately; actual dataset values may differ slightly
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer planar dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence at normal angle. Materials: HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) in alternating order starting with HfO2 at air side. Baseline thicknesses (all 24 layers): [122.0, 67.0, 135.0, 77.0, 105.0, 118.0, 43.0, 63.0, 142.0, 59.0, 110.0, 160.0, 44.0, 64.0, 164.0, 50.0, 116.0, 156.0, 123.0, 54.0, 185.0, 96.0, 51.0, 34.0] nm. Optimization strategy: Fix layers 0-14 and 22-23 at baseline values. Optimize only layers 15-21 (7 variables) using Nelder-Mead simplex with step bounds ±12 nm from baseline. Inject 2 uniform-random candidates per round (all 24 layers randomized within 20-200 nm) to maintain population diversity. Spectral targets: maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm, maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm, equal weighting. Use coherent transfer-matrix method. Total layer count fixed at 24. Materials resolved from catalog as hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand).
routes.revision_reason: Continuation of control_route_01 with constrained local search strategy: fixed outer layers 0-14 and 22-23 from best prior candidate, Nelder-Mead refinement on middle layers 15-21 with ±12 nm bounds, 2 random candidates per round for diversity. Based on feedback directive to test reflected deviation mechanism.

Optimal bound width for Nelder-Mead (±12 nm chosen from recalled practice; actual optimal may differ)

plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If this control route cannot exceed 0.825 target score after constrained local search, the limitation may be fundamental to the material pair or stack count rather than optimization strategy, and would require either more layers (up to 30) or alternative material combinations to突破.

expected_observations: best_target_score should increase beyond 0.818 if middle-layer refinement unlocks additional performance
valid_candidates should remain high (≥7) since fixed outer layers preserve physical validity of baseline topology
tightest_margin should not decrease significantly if constrained search stays near valid region
If best_target_score plateaus below 0.825 after 3 rounds, the middle-layer hypothesis may be insufficient and full-stack re-optimization would be needed
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the constrained subspace as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates falls below 5 for two consecutive rounds, relax the ±12 nm bound to ±20 nm and continue
if tightest_margin falls below 0.5 for two consecutive rounds, reduce random candidate injection rate from 2 to 1 per round and continue

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.
